description:
Experiment. mimalloc behind a cargo feature on fz-runtime, enabled only for the per-arm runtime staticlib (cargo rustc -p fz-runtime --crate-type staticlib) linked via FZ_AOT_RUNTIME_STATICLIB. fz2 links fz-runtime as an rlib without the feature and keeps the system allocator (Optimize's counting #[global_allocator] untouched); enabling it in fz2 fails at link time. Decides whether fz-9x7.12 needs fz code. Rules in cycles and page reclaims.

Plan: https://claude.ai/artifact/Pqqu5yTcQdBbkGsZyZiykb (GC memory plan v3, approved by the user 2026-11-17).

comments.text: Add an arm (GC session request, from fz-9x7.24): survive with the binary-destructor leak arm as the floor. It separates "two frees per binary" from "system malloc per-free cost" (fz-9x7.24 measured ~304 instructions / ~300 cycles per binary destruction, 14% of survive cycles, 200k destructions, two frees each: 1025-byte buffer + 48-byte SharedBin box). If mimalloc closes most of the gap, a one-allocation SharedBin layout is still a simplification but a smaller win.

Bench round (arms exp/9x7-22-mimalloc 0a6e6e612 on develop a6ae5759d, 25 interleaved runs, dist-full 9, outputs identical). Decision rule: B3M within 1.02x V0 in distiller cycles and 1.25x page reclaims => S not built. dist-full B3M: cycles 1.035, page reclaims 2.217 => FAILS, so S (fz-9x7.12) is built. Prediction ('partly: reclaims fall but stay well above V0') held: B3 alone reclaims 5.80x, B3M 2.22x. Side finding, capped arm VM vs V0 (cycles / instructions): survive 0.761/0.818, deadbinlive 0.794/0.844, msg 0.863/0.845, enum 1.031/1.014, distiller 1.000/1.002, others within ~1.7%. Max RSS: spin +29.5%, msg +13.7%, distiller +19.5%. survive/deadbinlive were measured before fz-9x7.25 (one-block binaries), which halves their malloc calls; msg allocates no binaries, so 14% of msg's cycles go to system malloc on some other per-message path.

Follow-up (GC, 2026-11-17): mimalloc cuts cycles 14-24% on survive/deadbinlive/msg at today's cap, where fz makes many small mallocs (two per binary before fz-9x7.25; a Box<ParkRecord> per park). B3M ~ VM wherever B3 does nothing, so the malloc effect and the young-cap effect are independent; on enum B3 is the whole win (cycles 0.85) and mimalloc adds nothing. Re-run VM against V0 after fz-9x7.25 and the per-park allocation fix (GC proposal B / Optimize receive-closure A) land: if little of the 14-24% remains, fz needed fewer malloc calls, not a different malloc. fz-9x7.12 (S) priority is unchanged: it owns young-gen large-block page faults, which mimalloc does not fix (2.2x reclaims).

title: Measure mimalloc as the global allocator for compiled programs against the system allocator (experiment)
